title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: Market participants weigh in on SEC’s proposed crypto regulations
summary: The financial agency is scheduled to close public comments on its ‘Regulation Crypto Assets’ proposed in August.

title: Visa, Mesh partner to enable crypto spending at 175M merchant locations
summary: Mesh will connect crypto and stablecoin wallets to Visa’s global payment network, allowing users to spend digital assets without a separate card.

title: Mastercard launches stablecoin risk screening for banks and payment providers
summary: The new service combines payment data and blockchain analytics to help banks detect suspicious stablecoin transactions before settlement.

title: Revolut secures Gibraltar crypto license to support global expansion
summary: The UK-based fintech will use the authorization to offer crypto services in additional international markets, though it has not disclosed specific countries or launch dates.

title: Metaplanet to take 93.7% stake in Super League through 2,100 BTC deal
summary: The transaction would give Metaplanet access to US capital markets, where it plans to use preferred stock offerings to finance additional Bitcoin purchases.

title: Strive buys $335M in Bitcoin, boosting holdings to 36,818 BTC
summary: The Bitcoin treasury company added another 1,223 BTC after an earlier purchase pushed it past MARA Holdings, while continuing to expand its reserves through equity financing.

title: Bitcoin is rejected at $83K as US bond yields reverse higher with equities
summary: Bitcoin price action failed to improve with equities as a sell wall at $83,000 kept BTC in a tight range.

title: Made an ‘honest’ mistake with crypto taxes? New bill offers way out
summary: A proposed US bill would let crypto investors correct past tax reporting mistakes through a dedicated disclosure program, with reduced penalties for eligible taxpayers.

title: Public companies object to OKX-ICE’s tokenized stock plan
summary: Nine public companies objected to having their shares offered in tokenized form by OKX and ICE, testing whether platforms can create blockchain-based markets without issuer consent.
